name: Microsoft for Education Daily
tldr: Excel on Windows is starting to explain formula errors, Teams Rooms will put your laptop on both screens, and Microsoft 365 Backup can keep OneDrive and SharePoint backups for up to ten years.
window: Window: the 24 hours to 07:40 AEDT, Thu 26 Nov 2026 (Wednesday 25 Nov in the US).
notes: A quiet day for education-specific news: no new Microsoft Education posts or [Education] roadmap items in the window, so today's stories are campus-wide updates framed for schools and universities.

Status: Excel's error cards and Copilot in read-only workbooks are rolling out; Teams Rooms dual-screen sharing and external bot reports (January) and SharePoint page templates (December) are roadmap items in development; the Windows memory savings are as Microsoft described them at Ignite 2026, reported by Windows Latest.
Screenshots are the publishers' public pages as captured on 26 Nov 2026; copyright remains with the publishers.

post.text:
LESS GUESSWORK. 🧩

The last 24h at Microsoft for education:
- Excel now explains formula errors (rolling out)
- Teams Rooms: your laptop on both screens (due Jan)
- 10-year backups for OneDrive and SharePoint
- Windows apps use less memory on 8 GB PCs (reported)
post.alt: A 3-minute motion-graphics showreel of Microsoft updates for education (26 Nov 2026): Excel's descriptive error cards, Teams Rooms sharing to both displays, Copilot in read-only Excel workbooks, faster chat in VS Code, ten-year recovery windows in Microsoft 365 Backup, Teams reports on external bots, SharePoint's organization-wide page templates, Microsoft's test of AI coding agents on contradictory docs, the sign-in issue after November's Windows updates, Microsoft's ARTEX warning, Windows apps using less memory and the first player to reach 10 million Gamerscore, with captions, sources and article screenshots.

stories.title: Excel on Windows now explains formula errors and how to fix them
stories.summary: Hover over a cell's error indicator and Excel explains what an error like #REF! or #VALUE! means, its likely causes and how to fix it; for supported errors, 'Fix this error' asks Copilot to repair the formula. Already in Excel for the web, it's rolling out to Excel for Windows (Version 2611 or later), handy for students learning formulas.
stories.for: Students and teachers working with formulas

stories.title: Teams Rooms on Android will show your shared laptop on both room displays
stories.summary: On Microsoft Teams Rooms on Android with dual displays, content shared over HDMI will be able to appear on both screens at once, even when you're not in a Teams meeting; you start or stop it from the room controls and admins manage the setting. It's a roadmap item in development, due January 2027. A lecture theatre with two screens is our example.
stories.for: Teachers in two-screen rooms, and campus AV and IT teams

stories.title: Copilot in Excel now works in read-only workbooks
stories.summary: You can now open Copilot in a read-only workbook and ask about it, such as what the data shows or which figures stand out. It's rolling out to Excel for Windows, Mac and the web and needs Copilot in Excel. A shared report from the school office is our example.
stories.for: Staff and teachers reading shared reports

stories.title: VS Code 1.148 starts chat answers about 30% faster
stories.summary: Visual Studio Code 1.148, released on 25 November, makes chat responses in the Agent Host begin about 30% faster on average than the previous Stable version. It can also keep a plugged-in PC awake while an agent works (a preview setting) and adds a Troubleshoot page for failed remote connections.
stories.for: Student coders and computer science classes

stories.title: Microsoft 365 Backup can now keep OneDrive and SharePoint recovery points for up to ten years
stories.summary: SharePoint and OneDrive backup policies now support recovery windows of 3 or 6 months, or any whole number of years from 1 to 10, up from a maximum of two. The one-year default is unchanged, single-file and folder restores only go back 14 days, and Exchange stays at up to two years; longer windows can raise costs, while restores stay free.
stories.for: School and university IT teams that use Microsoft 365 Backup

stories.title: Teams admins will be able to see which outside bots joined their meetings
stories.summary: A Microsoft 365 roadmap item in development, due January 2027, adds external bot detection and activity reports to the Teams admin center, so admins can track which external bots were detected in and got into meetings and events hosted in their tenant. Outside AI notetakers joining class or staff meetings are our example.
stories.for: School and university IT and Teams admins

stories.title: SharePoint is getting organization-wide page templates
stories.summary: Organizations will be able to offer reusable, approved page templates across all their SharePoint sites, managed centrally in the site linked to their brand center, so authors skip repetitive setup and pages stay consistent. It's a roadmap item in development, due December 2026. School and faculty news pages are our example.
stories.for: School comms teams and SharePoint admins

stories.title: When two docs pages disagree, AI coding agents often follow the wrong one
stories.summary: Microsoft tested three real contradictions from its Dev Proxy docs with three models in about 140 agent runs. Agents often noticed the pages disagreed but followed the wrong one first, and detours cost up to 38% more tokens. Agents that checked a second source weren't misled at all, a good habit for students too.
stories.for: Computer science teachers and student coders

stories.title: November's Windows security updates can break NTLM sign-ins with some third-party tools
stories.summary: Microsoft confirms November's security updates, the first phase of NTLM signing changes (CVE-2026-118737), can break authentication with some third-party apps and devices, such as authentication proxies, single sign-on and app-packaging tools. Its registry workaround is temporary; updating the product or using Kerberos is the long-term fix.

stories.title: Microsoft warns attackers are abusing ARTEX, an AI pen-testing tool
stories.summary: Microsoft Threat Intelligence says state-sponsored and financially motivated groups use ARTEX, an AI penetration testing framework released in July 2026, to automate attacks that can reach privileged access within minutes. It advises cutting internet exposure, securing secrets and credentials, and turning on automatic attack disruption in Defender XDR.

stories.title: Microsoft says its own apps now use less memory on Windows 11
stories.summary: At an Ignite 2026 session, as reported by Windows Latest, Microsoft said Microsoft 365 now uses about 360 MB less memory and Defender, Purview and OneDrive save over half a gigabyte combined, with a focus on 8 GB and 16 GB PCs; Windows Latest totals it at over 860 MB. Good news for 8 GB school laptops.
stories.for: School IT and anyone on an 8 GB or 16 GB laptop

stories.title: The first Xbox player to reach 10 million Gamerscore
stories.summary: Xbox Wire interviewed SiegfriedX, Brazilian player Marcello Malta, who reached 10 million Gamerscore on 9 September 2026, the first Xbox player to do it, after 20 years and more than 6,400 games. He has unlocked at least one achievement every day since 2020.

transcript.t: This is the Microsoft for Education Daily, for Thursday.
Here's your day in Microsoft updates, in 3 minutes flat.
Less guesswork for students: when a formula breaks, Excel on Windows now explains what went wrong.
Hover over the error for causes and fixes, or let Copilot repair it.
Lecture theatre with two screens?
Teams Rooms on Android will show your shared laptop on both, due January.
Plug in over HDMI and the back row sees it too, even outside a Teams meeting.
Opened a read-only report from the office?
Copilot in Excel now works there too, rolling out.
Student coders? This week's VS Code starts chat answers about 30% faster.
School IT?
Microsoft 365 Backup now keeps OneDrive and SharePoint backups up to ten years.
The default stays one year, single-file restores only go back 14 days, and Exchange stops at two.
Due January, Teams admins should see which outside bots turned up in their meetings and events.
And SharePoint gets organization-wide page templates, due December: approved starting points for school news pages.
Something calmer for coding classes: when two docs pages disagree, AI agents often follow the wrong one.
In Microsoft's test, agents that checked a second source weren't misled at all.
Good advice for students too.
The fine print?
November's Windows security updates can break sign-ins through some proxies and single sign-on tools.
And Microsoft warns attackers are abusing ARTEX, an AI pen-testing tool that can break in within minutes.
After hours, good news for 8 GB laptops: Microsoft says its own apps now use less memory.
Office uses 360 MB less; Defender, Purview and OneDrive save over half a gig.
On Xbox, a Brazilian player is the first to hit 10 million Gamerscore, after 20 years.
Clearer errors, lighter laptops, longer backups: a little less guesswork all round.
Day after day, the updates keep stacking up.
Some of it's shipped. The rest is on its way.
One day, all of this. Tomorrow, probably more.
This has been the Microsoft for Education Daily.
See you tomorrow.
